notes: Monitoring inventory for native Claude Code marketplace plugins. It ships EMPTY and G1.1 installs no plugin: `plugins` is [] and every check over it is a no-op. The schema exists so that adopting a plugin later is a reviewed data change rather than monitoring invented under time pressure. It is read by scripts/skill_updates/plugins.py and consumed by scripts/validate-agent-governance.py (--self-test) as the canonical empty plugin inventory. The stable-owned G1.1 workflow is artifact-only and UNCOMMISSIONED while main remains the repository default; it cannot install, update, or publish a plugin. Full detail: docs/agents/skills-update-automation.md.

surfaces.A_project_skills: Repo-vendored skills under .claude/skills/**, governed by docs/agents/<provider>-skills-manifest.json and updated by the candidate flow. This is the surface the update bot acts on.
surfaces.B_native_plugins: Marketplace plugins installed by Claude Code into a user cache OUTSIDE this repository. This file monitors them. The bot never runs `claude plugin update`, never installs Claude Code in CI, and never mutates a real plugin cache.
surfaces.C_claudeai_zip_skills: Custom skills packaged as a ZIP and uploaded through the claude.ai web interface. There is no documented programmatic upload, so this project treats surface C as documentation and package output only. Nothing is automated for it.

auto_update_policy: Anthropic's own marketplaces auto-update by default; third-party marketplaces default to auto-update OFF. An updated plugin is not live in a running session until /reload-plugins or a new session — the session keeps whatever it loaded at startup. For any project-governed audited plugin, native silent auto-update should be DISABLED so changes arrive through the monitored candidate flow and get a human audit, exactly as vendored skills do.
audit_required_on: any version change, from any precedence source
an unchanged version over a changed source commit (the dangerous direction: the label proves nothing about the bytes)
source repository, source ref, or marketplace change
any component-surface change: skills, agents, hooks, mcp_servers, lsp_servers, monitors, bin, settings, dependencies
a change in projected context cost
a plugin installed but absent from this inventory
